Remember one line: RV repair is difficult because systems intersect. A leak can result from an aging pipe or a failed pump, requiring both plumbing and electrical checks. Experience matters more than manuals.

It does not suit people who dislike dirt, are careless, or only perform one type of work. RVs have confined spaces and contain water, electricity, and gas, requiring bent-over disassembly. Forgetting one wire can cause an accident on the owner's trip.

A common path is: automotive / electromechanical education or apprenticeship → build water-system and chassis experience at an RV dealership or repair shop → earn electrical, refrigeration, and related certificates → master RV-specific water, electrical, gas, and air-conditioning systems → advance toward customization technician, after-sales supervisor, or shop owner.
This career suits hands-on people willing to learn everything. You need plumbing, electrical, and gas skills and patience with diagnosis. RV faults often cross several systems and cannot be rushed.

Recreational Vehicle Service Technicians inspect, repair, maintain, and customize RVs, campers, and similar vehicles. They troubleshoot water, electrical, gas, air-conditioning and heating, generator, chassis, and interior systems to ensure safe, reliable operation.

paragraphs: A typical day centers on checking systems, removing components, and testing functions. Review work orders in the morning and first handle urgent leaks and unusual noises. Troubleshooting often requires eliminating water and electrical causes one by one before disassembly and repair. Afternoons involve maintenance and customization, followed by system-by-system testing. Peak season brings one vehicle after another; slow season focuses on deep maintenance and preparation.

In one line: repair and test every RV system. Duties include water, electrical, and gas repairs, air-conditioner and generator maintenance, chassis inspection, customization, system testing, and work-order records.

paragraphs: A score of 4/10 means RV service is a hands-on technical role with low-to-moderate AI exposure. Manuals, parts, and diagnostic assistance become digital, while disassembly, repair, and field tuning depend on people. AI searches information and people perform repairs, so near-term replacement risk is low; the main risk is insufficient breadth of skills.

Moderately high exposure does not allow workers to stop learning. As RV systems become more electronic, technicians should read fault codes, use diagnostic equipment, and understand electronic controls. Upgrading from mechanical repairer to intelligent RV technician creates a major difference in peak-season capacity.

Students in automotive or electromechanical programs can consider the RV niche. The industry is growing, competition is lower than traditional auto repair, and broad skills are rewarded. Build foundations in plumbing, electrical work, refrigeration, and electronics, and intern at an RV manufacturer or repair shop during school breaks.

Learn all six major RV systems: water, electrical, gas, air conditioning, generator, and chassis. Earn electrical and refrigeration certificates and expand into customization and after-sales management. Take customization jobs in peak season and perform preparation and maintenance in slow season for healthier income.

People with automotive, plumbing, electrical, or refrigeration backgrounds have clear advantages. Add RV-specific systems knowledge and begin in an after-sales workshop. Emphasize combined water, electrical, and gas capabilities and field troubleshooting cases rather than simply saying you repair vehicles.

RV repair talent is difficult to recruit and slow to develop, so build an apprenticeship system. Hire beginners with automotive backgrounds, systematically teach RV water, electrical, and gas systems, provide strong diagnostic equipment, and retain workers through combined-skill allowances + customization commissions.

Recreational vehicle service technicians primarily work at RV dealership after-sales workshops, specialized repair shops, and customization facilities. They inspect, repair, and customize water, electrical, gas, air-conditioning, generator, chassis, and interior systems, with strong seasonal demand swings.
Median wage and employment projections from BLS OOH; wage distribution from BLS OES 2025 (collected 2026)
The distinctive reward is protecting other people's travel. When an owner says they trust your work and vehicle after vehicle departs during peak season, you know each carries a family's vacation.

The most interesting part is that every vehicle differs. An RV is a small mobile apartment containing water, electricity, gas, air conditioning, and entertainment. Today you repair plumbing, tomorrow diagnose wiring, and the next day install solar, creating varied work that never becomes dull.
If you enjoy the tangible feeling that repairing one vehicle serves one family and are willing to combine water, electrical, and gas expertise, RV repair is a growing technical field.
